description: First-time onboarding: companion derives Early stage from conversational cues (loss of financial/medication management, preserved self-awareness) and initiates LCWS baseline

conversation.content: Welcome to Lantern. I'm here to help you navigate caring for your mother. Before I can give you stage-aware guidance, I'd like to ask a few questions about where she is right now — this usually takes about 10 minutes. Is now a good time?
Yes, I have a few minutes.
Thank you for being here. Let's start with some day-to-day things. Is your mother still managing her own finances — paying bills, handling her bank account?
No, she stopped being able to do that about six months ago. I take care of all of that now.
That's a significant shift to take on. How about familiar tasks at home — cooking, doing laundry, keeping up with her medications?
She can't manage her meds on her own anymore, and she's given up cooking. She still gets around the house okay though.
Is she still aware of who she is, who you are, and where she is — even if her memory isn't what it used to be?
Yes, she knows who I am. She has bad days but she's generally aware of herself and her surroundings.

Based on what you've described — loss of ability to manage finances and medications, relying on help with daily tasks, but still aware of herself and her surroundings — your mother sounds like she's in the Early stage of dementia. Does that feel accurate to you?
Yes, that sounds right. Her neurologist said something similar.
Good — that helps me give you guidance that actually fits where you are. Before we go further, I want to check in on you. How are you doing in all of this?

That makes a lot of sense. You're carrying a lot. I'd like to ask a few more questions about how this is affecting different areas of your life — just to get a baseline so I can track how you're doing over time. Is that okay?
